newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 7.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 7.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Westpac Banking Corp must show that its proposed merger with the Bank of Melbourne Ltd does not lessen competition, Allan Fels chairman of Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Sunday. "They will certainly have to show there is no reduction in competition, that is the challenge they face," Fels said in a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday Business show.

Australian coal miner CIM Resources Ltd said on Sunday it had extended the term of the existing subscription agreement with British coal miner RJB Mining Plc by 18 months. CIM said under the new agreement RJB would have the right to subscribe A$113.6 million for a further 110 million shares until December 1998. Under the existing agreement, RJB subscribed A$22.5 million for 25 million shares or 12.5 percent of CIM's issued capital.

CanWest Global Communications Corp said on Friday it would explore mutually acceptable options to rectify what the Australian Broadcast Authority called a breach in foreign ownership rules in connection with CanWest's control of Australia's Ten television network. CanWest said it was surprised by the ABA ruling.
Biota Holdings Ltd on Monday it has signed an agreement with La Trobe University, Melbourne, for the exclusive worldwide rights to newly synthesised anti-cancer chemical compounds.

Bendigo Bank Ltd said on Friday it expected a lower core pre-tax profit for the year to June 30, 1997, due to a delcine in revenue from home lending. However, the regional bank said its annual profit after-tax should not be significantly different from a year ago, although there would be additional abnormal expenses to complete the restructuring of Monte Paschi's Australian subsidiary.

Bank of Queensland Ltd said on Friday there was evidence of a significant turnaround in new lending approvals in the current half year. Bank of Queensland earlier announced a 21.7 percent fall in net profit for the six months to February 28.
